fish-bass-baked-or-broiled-coated.title: Fish, bass, baked or broiled, coated

content.title: About
content.content: Bass is a freshwater fish from the perch family, prized for its tender white flesh, low fat content, and mild flavor. When baked or broiled with a coating, the fish stays moist while the crust adds a satisfying crunch.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Bass can grow up to 60 cm and weigh over 2 kg, but most market portions are fillets of 150–250 g.
Coatings often combine breadcrumbs, flour, herbs, and spices to enhance aroma and texture.
Baking at 180–200 °C preserves most B‑vitamins, while quick broiling creates a golden crust.
Bass is commonly served with lemon, fresh herbs (parsley, dill) and a light yogurt or cream sauce.
In many households bass is considered a “go‑to” fish because of its availability and ease of preparation.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Bass provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Less than 2 g of fat per 100 g, mostly polyunsaturated.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B12, B6 and niacin aid nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals: selenium and phosphorus
items.content: Selenium acts as an antioxidant; phosphorus is essential for bones and teeth.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Although lower than in fatty fish, bass still supplies EPA and DHA.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Freshwater bass can accumulate cadmium or mercury, so moderate consumption is advised.

items.title: High sodium in coating
items.content: Salty breading can increase sodium intake, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Proper cooking
items.content: Undercooked fish may harbor pathogens; cook to an internal temperature of 63 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Coat bass fillets in a mixture of breadcrumbs, spices, and a drizzle of olive oil, then bake 15–20 minutes at 200 °C or broil until golden. Serve with lemon wedges, fresh herbs, and a light vegetable side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh fillets in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C for up to 2 days in an airtight container. Frozen fillets store at –18 °C for up to 3 months. Thaw frozen fish in the fridge, not at room temperature.

hot-dog-sandwich-meat-and-poultry-on-whe.title: Hot dog sandwich, meat and poultry, on wheat bread

content.title: About
content.content: A hot dog sandwich consists of a meat‑and‑poultry sausage placed inside a split wheat bun. It is a popular fast‑food item often served with mustard, ketchup, mayonnaise and various vegetable toppings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first hot dog appeared in the United States in the late 19th century and quickly became street food.
Traditional American hot dogs are served in a wheat‑flour bun, but many countries use different types of bread.
There are more than 50 varieties of sausages used in hot dogs, including beef, pork, chicken and turkey.
In 1945 the first "National Hot Dog Day" was celebrated in the US, now observed annually.
Hot dogs are closely associated with baseball games and festivals.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Meat and poultry sausage provides complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat products are rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The sausage supplies B12, B6 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the bun and fats from the sausage delivers quick energy.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: Protein, fat and carbs together help maintain a feeling of fullness for longer.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Processed sausages often contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: A high amount of saturated fat may contribute to cardiovascular disease when consumed frequently.

items.title: Preservatives and additives
items.content: Some sausages contain nitrites and other preservatives that are undesirable in large amounts.

items.title: Allergy to meat or gluten
items.content: People with allergies to certain meats or gluten may experience reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Hot dogs are calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hot dogs are usually eaten warm, topped with mustard, ketchup, mayonnaise, pickles, onions, cheese or salad. They can be heated on a grill, in an oven or in a microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared hot dog in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C for no more than 2 days. Keep the sausage in its original packaging or an airtight container, and the bun in a dry place to prevent it from drying out.

pretzels-soft-ready-to-eat-cinnamon-suga.title: Soft Pretzels, Ready‑to‑Eat, Cinnamon Sugar Coated

content.title: About
content.content: Soft pretzels are a ready‑to‑eat baked snack coated with a cinnamon‑sugar mixture. They are tender inside, slightly crisp outside, and have a sweet‑spicy aroma. Convenient for on‑the‑go consumption, they require no further preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic pretzel shape dates back to medieval monasteries, symbolizing crossed arms in prayer.
Soft pretzels are a popular treat at movie theaters and fairs.
The cinnamon‑sugar coating enhances aroma and appeals especially to children.
In the United States, sweet soft pretzels gained popularity in the 1970s with the rise of fast‑food chains.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Pretzels provide quickly digestible carbs that can give an immediate energy boost.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: A modest amount of fiber supports digestive health.

items.title: Antioxidants from cinnamon
items.content: Cinnamon is rich in polyphenols that have antioxidant properties.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of tooth decay.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Pretzels made from wheat flour contain gluten and are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Allergy to additives
items.content: Some versions may contain flavorings or preservatives that can trigger allergic reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, paired with yogurt or ice cream, or used in dessert recipes. They are easy to pack in a bag or backpack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store soft pretzels in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. For longer storage keep them refrigerated, though they may lose some softness.
